retrieval_cases.question: What actions count as a football act after controlling a pass?
When does losing the ball while going to the ground make a pass incomplete?
Is a pass automatically incomplete whenever the ball touches the ground?
Can a defensive penalty award the offense a new series?
What conditions make a forward pass legal?
How can a passer outside the pocket avoid intentional grounding?
Which offensive positions are eligible receivers?
He secures the pass, taps both toes inbounds, turns upfield, and only then loses the ball. Was the reception already completed?
A pressured quarterback escapes the tackle box and sails the throw past the original line of scrimmage with nobody nearby. Can that avoid grounding?
For a receiver at the goal line, how do the completed-catch requirements and the touchdown rule work together?
On fourth down, a runner fumbles before the line to gain and a teammate recovers beyond it. Which rule areas must be resolved to decide whether the offense earned a new series?
The offense committed a foul with 30 seconds left in the half. Is there a ten-second runoff?
A receiver lost the ball as he hit the ground. Was the pass complete?

evidence.document_title: Completing a Catch
evidence.text:
For a forward pass to be complete, an inbounds player must first control the ball before it touches
the ground. The player must then touch the ground inbounds with both feet, or with another body part
other than the hands. After those requirements, the player must perform an act common to the game or
maintain control long enough to perform one.

Examples of a football act include taking an additional step, tucking the ball and turning upfield,
extending the ball, or avoiding an opponent.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

Forward movement and loss of control
evidence.text:
An intentional forward movement of the passer's hand begins a forward pass. If contact causes the
passer to lose the ball after that movement begins, the play is treated as a pass. If the passer loses
the ball while pulling it back toward the body to re-cock the arm, it is a fumble.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

evidence.document_title: Forward Passes, Backward Passes, and Fumbles
heading_path: Forward Passes, Backward Passes, and Fumbles
evidence.text:
The offense may throw one forward pass during a down, and the pass must be released from behind the
line of scrimmage. Once the ball has crossed the line of scrimmage, the offense cannot bring it back
behind the line and then throw a forward pass.

A pass is illegal when it is a second forward pass, is released after a change of possession, or is
released when the passer's entire body and the ball are beyond the line of scrimmage. The exact
penalty depends on which restriction was violated.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

evidence.document_title: Completing a Catch
evidence.text:
If the player has control and gets two feet or another qualifying body part down but has neither
performed a football act nor maintained control long enough to perform one, losing control when
contacting the ground makes the pass incomplete. The
player does not need to keep control through the ground after all elements of the catch were already
completed; a later loss can instead be a fumble.

The ball may touch the ground without forcing an incompletion when the player maintains control and
the ground does not cause the loss of control.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

evidence.document_title: Receiver Eligibility and Illegal Touching
evidence.text:
An eligible offensive receiver who goes out of bounds before or during a pass becomes ineligible to
be the first player to touch that pass, even after reestablishing inbounds. If the receiver is the
first to touch or catch the pass after returning, illegal touching applies.

Whether the receiver went out voluntarily or was legally forced out can affect other parts of the
play, but neither circumstance automatically restores eligibility to touch the pass first.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

answer_cases.ruling: After a player first controls a forward pass, a football act is any action common to the game that the player performs or maintains control long enough to perform. Examples include taking an additional step, tucking the ball and turning upfield, extending the ball, or avoiding an opponent.
answer_cases.explanation: The rule states that once a player has control of a forward pass, the player must perform an act common to the game or maintain control long enough to perform one. The examples given are taking an additional step, tucking the ball and turning upfield, extending the ball, or avoiding an opponent.

evidence.text:
Intentional grounding can occur when a passer facing an imminent loss of yardage throws a forward
pass without a realistic eligible receiver in its direction and vicinity. A passer who has been
outside the pocket avoids grounding by throwing the ball to or beyond the line of scrimmage, even if
no receiver has a realistic chance to catch it. Other exceptions and timing rules may affect the
ruling, so the passer's location, pressure, target, and landing point all matter.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

A fumble is a loss of player possession that is not a pass or kick. The ball ordinarily remains live,
and either team may recover it. Special restrictions govern which offensive player may advance a
fumble on fourth down or after the two-minute warning, so a ruling in either situation requires those
additional facts.

evidence.document_title: Forward Passes, Backward Passes, and Fumbles
heading_path: Forward Passes, Backward Passes, and Fumbles
evidence.text:
A pass is backward when it first touches a player or the ground at a yard line parallel to or behind
the point where it left the passer's hand. A backward pass that hits the ground remains live and may
be recovered and advanced by either team. A snap is a backward pass.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

answer_cases.ruling: No, a pass is not automatically incomplete whenever the ball touches the ground.
answer_cases.explanation: The rules state that a forward pass must be controlled before it touches the ground to be complete (chunk 0a20866cb0efeb92). If the ball touches the ground after control has been established, the pass is incomplete only if the player loses control or fails to perform a football act (chunk 728ecff588868d07). Moreover, a backward pass that hits the ground remains live and can be recovered (chunk 0fefac6cd902f3c8). Thus, the ball touching the ground alone does not automatically make a pass incomplete; it depends on control and other factors.

evidence.document_title: Downs, Series, and the Line to Gain
heading_path: Downs, Series, and the Line to Gain
evidence.text:
The offense ordinarily receives a series of four scrimmage downs. It earns a new series when the
ball is declared dead in its possession at or beyond the line to gain. A defensive penalty can also
produce a new series by moving the ball to the line to gain or by awarding an automatic first down.

The forward-most point of the ball when it becomes dead is used when measuring whether the line to
gain was reached.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

evidence.document_title: Downs, Series, and the Line to Gain
heading_path: Downs, Series, and the Line to Gain
evidence.text:
If the offense has not reached the line to gain by the end of fourth down, the opponent receives a
new series. The next possession begins at the dead-ball spot after any accepted penalties are
enforced.

A change of possession during a play can produce a new series for the team that possesses the ball
at the end of the down. Interceptions and recovered fumbles are common examples.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

evidence.document_title: Receiver Eligibility and Illegal Touching
evidence.text:
A player wearing an ordinarily ineligible number can report to the referee as eligible for a play.
The player must then occupy an eligible position in a legal formation. Reporting changes the
player's declared status; it does not excuse an illegal alignment.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

evidence.document_title: Clock Management and Ten-Second Runoffs
evidence.text:
After the two-minute warning of either half, the offense cannot conserve time through specified
illegal acts while the clock is running. Examples include intentional grounding, an illegal forward
pass, throwing a backward pass out of bounds, or illegally batting or kicking the ball out of
bounds.

The usual consequence for an offensive act that illegally conserves time is the applicable yardage
penalty plus a ten-second runoff. The play clock is reset to 30 seconds and the game clock starts on
the ready-for-play signal. The offense can use an available timeout instead of the runoff, and the
defense can decline the runoff. A runoff can end the half.
evidence.source_title: 2026 Official Playing Rules of the National Football League

answer_cases.ruling: Yes, a defensive penalty can award the offense a new series.
answer_cases.explanation: According to the rule, a defensive penalty can produce a new series by moving the ball to the line to gain or by awarding an automatic first down.

answer_cases.ruling: A forward pass is legal when it is the offense’s first forward pass of the down, the ball is released from behind the line of scrimmage, the passer’s entire body and the ball are not beyond the line at the moment of release, and the pass is not made after a change of possession. The pass must also be initiated by an intentional forward movement of the passer’s hand.
answer_cases.explanation: The evidence states that the offense may throw one forward pass during a down and that the pass must be released from behind the line of scrimmage (chunk 0f214c9be67378d7). It also says a pass is illegal if it is a second forward pass, released after a change of possession, or released when the passer’s entire body and the ball are beyond the line of scrimmage (chunk 0f214c9be67378d7). Finally, the pass must be initiated by an intentional forward movement of the passer’s hand (chunk f863dc681ed93e5b). Combining these facts gives the conditions that make a forward pass legal.
